candidate.educational_objective: For a client receiving intra-arterial iodinated contrast, anticipate discontinuing metformin at or before the imaging procedure, re-evaluating eGFR 48 hours afterward, and restarting metformin only if renal function is stable.

options.A: Continue metformin and reassess eGFR 48 hours after the procedure only if oliguria develops.
options.B: Discontinue metformin at or before the procedure, reassess eGFR 48 hours later, and restart if renal function is stable.
options.C: Discontinue metformin only when the preprocedure eGFR is 30–60 mL/min/1.73 m²; otherwise continue it.
options.D: Continue metformin through the procedure if adequate hydration is maintained and reassess renal function afterward.

candidate.rationale: The current metformin prescribing information instructs discontinuation at the time of or before iodinated contrast imaging in patients who will receive intra-arterial iodinated contrast. eGFR should be re-evaluated 48 hours after the imaging procedure, and metformin should be restarted if renal function is stable. Therefore B is the best answer. A and D incorrectly continue metformin despite the intra-arterial contrast criterion. C incorrectly makes discontinuation depend only on the eGFR 30–60 mL/min/1.73 m² criterion even though intra-arterial contrast is itself a listed criterion for discontinuation.
